extracted.intended_audience: researchers generating or reporting microarray experiments and peer reviewers evaluating genomics/transcriptomics manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for the minimum information that must be recorded and reported for microarray-based gene expression experiments so data are interpretable and results independently verifiable. Used by data submitters to prepare datasets and by reviewers/journals/funders to assess compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raw data for each assay
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw data for each assay (e.g., CEL or GPR files).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the unprocessed output files from the scanner/instrument for every array/assay so others can reproduce processing choices; examples given include CEL and GPR file types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final processed (normalized) data
rubrics_metrics.description: Final processed (normalized) data for the set of assays in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the fully processed data used for analysis (normalized expression values) for the complete set of assays so results can be checked; document the exact form of the processed matrix provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential sample annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Essential sample annotation including experimental factors and their values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and report metadata for each sample such as treatment, time point, biological source, replicate identifiers, and the explicit values of experimental factors to enable interpretation and reanalysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental design including sample data relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the overall study design (e.g., case/control, time series), how samples relate to assays, blocking, randomization, and any pairing so statistical analysis and conclusions can be validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation of array features
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient annotation of array features (e.g., gene identifiers, sequence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide mappings from array probes/features to gene identifiers, probe sequences, annotations, and any feature-level metadata to allow interpretation of probe-level signals and cross-platform comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory and data processing protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Essential laboratory and data processing protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document wet-lab protocols (sample preparation, labeling, hybridization) and all data-processing steps (background correction, normalization, summarization, software/versions, parameter settings) so analyses are reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raw data deposited in public repository
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw data deposited in public repository (GEO, ArrayExpress).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a reviewer check that the submitter has deposited raw (and ideally processed) data in a recognized public repository such as GEO or ArrayExpress and provided accession numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate sample annotation (reviewer check)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should verify that sample metadata are sufficiently detailed and structured to link samples to experimental factors and assays; lack of adequate annotation should be flagged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducible data processing pipeline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should confirm that the data-processing pipeline is described with enough detail (tools, versions, parameters) to allow independent reproduction of normalized/processed results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with MIAME requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess that the submission is consistent with MIAME elements overall (raw data, processed data, annotation, design, features, protocols) and request missing items when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and awareness of related minimum-information standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Related standards (MINSEQE, MIAME extensions, MIAPE, MIBBI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of and, where appropriate, apply related or domain-specific minimum-information standards such as MINSEQE for sequencing, MIAME extensions (MIAME-env, MIAME-nut, MIAME-tox), MIAPE for proteomics, or umbrella standards (MIBBI) when the experiment spans modalities or specific domains.
